Concentrated triage batch: `finding` → `pm:queue`, **Bug**, S (`domain:devx` stands) — the scan's own stated invariant ("the escape verdict is a lower bound") is violated: `PATH_LITERAL` matches a backtick template with interpolation, so `${someVar}` walks as ONE descent and biases the verdict upward. Fix: make an interpolating template take the documented cannot-read path (no name, depth preserved); pin both directions in the self-test.

Strengthening needs no maintainer; weakening would. |

**Premise re-verified against `origin/main` = `402113d57`**, not against the card body (filed 2026-08-23 against `7f30b6be`):

```
557:const PATH_LITERAL = /^(['"`])([^'"`]*)\1$/;
653:    const lit = a.match(PATH_LITERAL);
```

Unchanged, and the character class still excludes only quote characters — so a backtick template with no quotes inside it matches, exactly as the card measured. Positive controls: the file reads at 2250 lines, and a search for an existing interpolation guard returns **zero** hits, so nothing has been fixed under the card since it was filed.

**Serial constraints.** No hot-file collision. `scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` is not in this seat's serial queue and no in-flight claim touches it. ⚠️ One adjacency worth knowing: this gate is a *dependency* of several other gate derivations (`check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` derives through it), so a change here can move other gates' family lists — which is why the derived list below is larger than the one file suggests.

**Fold-or-serial:** not folded with anything. No other queued card in this lane touches this file.

---

Dispatching now with the two dispositions already narrowed to one by triage's grade, and with `PATH_LITERAL`'s **second** call site (line 653 is one of at least two uses) flagged as the thing to measure before changing the constant.

## ACCEPT — PR #12087

Reviewer of record: devx seat, `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6` (seat #6023). All **31** check runs `completed`, grouped by name, latest per name — 0 failures. `Lint & Repo Gates` success at 08:28:50Z, `Type Check · workspace` at 08:30:05Z.

### My Zone 2.2 caution was checked and came out negative — which is the right outcome for a caution

I flagged the main risk as `PATH_LITERAL` being a module-level constant with **multiple consumers**, and said a fix that silently changed an unrelated consumer's verdict would be worse than the defect. The dev grepped before touching it and found exactly one call site. I verified that myself on `origin/main` rather than accepting it:

```
557:const PATH_LITERAL = /^(['"`])([^'"`]*)\1$/;
653:    const lit = a.match(PATH_LITERAL);
```

Definition plus one use, inside `pathExpression()`'s `resolve`/`join` argument walk. So narrowing moves no other consumer — and the dev routed it through a `readablePathLiteral()` wrapper at the call site anyway rather than mutating the shared constant, which keeps the constant's meaning intact for anything added later. That is the more conservative of the two shapes I offered, chosen with the measurement in hand.

### ⭐ Zone 2.3 came back in the stronger direction

I asked whether the fix makes the file's sentence true **at the resolver**, or merely keeps relying on the downstream filter — and said either was shippable, only an unexamined claim was not.

It is now true at the resolver. Before the fix, *"never a wrong name"* held only because `findEscapingPackages()`'s `statSync(...).isFile()` filter happened to drop the fabricated roster entry — a filesystem accident standing in for a parser invariant. After it, `pathExpression()` never produces a name for an interpolating template in the first place. The claim is now made where the comment makes it.

### The spin-off is better scoped than a copy would have been

`NEW_URL_LITERAL` sits three lines above `PATH_LITERAL` with the identical `[^'"`]*` character class. I confirmed both on `origin/main` (558 def / 641 use). The dev filed it as **#12085** rather than riding it in — and, more usefully, refused to assume this card's disposition transfers:

> an unmatched `NEW_URL_LITERAL` does not fall into an explicit "cannot read, keep depth" branch … the consequence of matching a template today is not "wrong depth kept" so much as "the whole seed is silently misread instead of being silently unrecognised" — worth its own triage read.

⭐ That distinction is real and is the kind of thing a copy-the-fix rider would have flattened. #12085 is also honest about what it did **not** check ("whether that filter also catches this shape was not re-verified here"), which is what makes it usable by whoever grades it. Filed unassigned and unlabelled — correct; grading is triage's field.

### Non-vacuity is demonstrated, not asserted
Reverting the call site to the raw `a.match(PATH_LITERAL)` — with the fix commit intact, so a real restore point exists — fails **exactly the two** new assertions and none of the others (`2/113`). Restored and `git diff HEAD` confirmed clean before re-running. The four added cases include the control the narrowing could otherwise overshoot: a **non-interpolating** backtick literal is still read normally and still correctly named.

`bare-root-worklist --self-test` unaffected, as predicted — no new scan root. `skip-changeset` correct: one gate script under root `scripts/`, nothing published.

Landing now: flip ready, arm SQUASH, verify by the queue ref.
